title: Route Parameters aur Constraints
objectives: Required aur optional route parameters likhna
Ek se zyada parameters aur unka order samajhna

sections.heading: Route parameter kya hota hai?
sections.body: URL ke dynamic hisse ko parameter kehte hain. `/users/{id}` mein `{id}` kuch bhi ho sakta hai, aur woh value closure ya controller method ko mil jaati hai.

code.code:
<?php

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;

Route::get('/users/{id}', function (string $id) {
    return "User #{$id}";
});

Route::get('/users/{user}/posts/{post}', function (string $user, string $post) {
    return "User {$user}, Post {$post}";
});

explain: `{id}` – required parameter. URL mein na ho to route match nahi hota (404).
Parameters ka naam sirf letters aur `_` ho sakta hai.
Parameters **order** ke hisaab se inject hote hain, naam se nahi. Pehla `{user}` pehla argument banta hai.

sections.heading: Real-world example: Blog aur orders
sections.body: Blog mein `/posts/{slug}` jahan slug `laravel-routing` jaisa hota hai. Orders mein `/orders/{id?}` jahan id na ho to saare orders dikhao.
explain: `{id?}` – optional parameter. Function mein default value zaroor do (`= null`).
Optional parameter hamesha last mein rakho.

sections.heading: Constraints: parameter ko restrict karna
sections.body: Bina constraint ke `{id}` mein `abc` bhi chal jaata hai. Constraint lagane se galat format par seedha 404 aata hai.

sections.heading: Global constraint: Route::pattern()
sections.body: Agar har jagah `{id}` numeric hona chahiye, to ek baar `AppServiceProvider::boot()` mein pattern set kar do.

callout.text: Route parameter mein `/` by default allow nahi hota. Agar chahiye to `->where('search', '.*')` use karo, par yeh sirf last parameter ke liye kaam karta hai.

sections.heading: Controller mein parameters
sections.body: Controller method mein pehle dependencies (jaise `Request`), phir route parameters likho.

versionDiff.heading: Version notes
versionDiff.intro: Parameters aur constraints ka behaviour teeno versions mein same hai.

errors.cause: `whereNumber('id')` ki wajah se non-numeric value match nahi hui.

errors.error: Missing required parameter for [Route: users.show] [URI: users/{id}] [Missing parameter: id]
Galat value mil rahi hai (user ki jagah post ki id)
errors.cause: Closure ya method ke arguments ka order route parameters ke order se alag hai.
errors.fix: Arguments ko URL ke parameters ke order mein likho.

debug.body: Parameters aur constraints `route:list` mein dikhte hain.

code.code:
php artisan route:list --path=users
php artisan route:list --path=posts

exercise.intro: Yeh routes banao aur browser mein test karo:
tasks: `/posts/{slug}` jahan slug sirf lowercase letters, numbers aur `-` ho

quiz.why: Naam ke baad `?` lagate hain aur function mein default value dete hain.

quiz.q: Route parameters function mein kaise inject hote hain?
quiz.why: Parameters URL ke order mein arguments ban jaate hain.

quiz.q: `whereNumber('id')` galat value par kya hota hai?
quiz.why: Constraint match na ho to route match hi nahi hota, isliye 404.

interview.a: Parameter ke liye allowed format, jaise `where('id', '[0-9]+')` ya `whereNumber('id')`.

interview.q: Optional parameter ke saath kya dhyan rakhna chahiye?
interview.a: Function mein default value dena zaroori hai aur optional parameter last mein hona chahiye.
Ek parameter naam ke liye global constraint set karta hai, jo sab routes par lagta hai.

interview.q: Route parameters ka order kyun matter karta hai?
interview.a: Laravel parameters ko naam se nahi, URL ke order se closure/controller ke arguments mein bharta hai.

interview.q: Parameter mein `/` kaise allow karte hain?
interview.a: `->where('search', '.*')` se, par sirf last parameter mein.

summary: Parameters order se inject hote hain.
Controller mein dependencies pehle, route parameters baad mein.
